input: Commission a custom illustration for the living room wall

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The subject matter and theme of the illustration (e.g. landscape, portrait, abstract, family scene) fundamentally shapes what kind of artist to seek and what brief to write.
The budget determines which tier of artist is realistic, whether to use a platform vs. a direct referral, and what size or complexity is feasible.
The intended display format — printed canvas, framed print, original on paper, painted directly on the wall — changes the deliverable the artist must produce and how the commission is structured.
The physical dimensions of the wall space constrain the artwork's size and aspect ratio, which the artist needs to know from the start.
The desired visual style (e.g. watercolour, line art, digital, oil-painting aesthetic) determines which artists are a match and guides the creative brief.
Knowing whether the user already has an artist in mind or needs help finding one changes whether the plan starts with sourcing/vetting or jumps straight to briefing.
The deadline or any event the artwork needs to be ready for (e.g. a housewarming, holiday gift) sets the urgency and determines how much revision time is realistic.

gold.taskTitle: Commission a custom illustration for living room
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to hire an artist to create a custom illustration to be displayed on their living room wall.

questions.title: What subject or theme should the illustration depict?
questions.description: Establish the core content of the artwork — e.g. a family portrait, a specific cityscape, a nature scene, something abstract — so the brief and artist search can be targeted.

questions.title: What is your total budget for this commission?
questions.description: Determine the financial ceiling to identify the right tier of artist, platform, and level of complexity that is achievable.

questions.title: How do you want the artwork physically displayed on the wall?
questions.description: Clarify the end format — e.g. an original piece, a printed canvas, a large framed print, or a mural — since this dictates the file type or medium the artist must deliver.

questions.title: What are the approximate dimensions of the wall space?
questions.description: Capture the available width and height so the artwork's size and aspect ratio can be specified in the commission brief from the outset.

questions.title: What visual style or artistic medium are you drawn to?
questions.description: Identify the aesthetic direction — e.g. watercolour, bold digital illustration, detailed pencil line art, a painterly oil style — to narrow the search to matching artists.

questions.title: Do you already have an artist in mind, or do you need to find one?
questions.description: Determine whether the plan begins with sourcing and vetting artists or can skip straight to drafting the brief and initiating contact.

questions.title: Is there a date by which the artwork must be ready?
questions.description: Establish any hard deadline — such as a housewarming, birthday, or holiday — to set the project timeline and build in realistic revision rounds.
